CAFETERIA LESSON · CAFETERIA · AGES 2–5 YEARS

Soup — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches soup as the bowl that came with rules — blow first, fish one at a time — and the oldest cooking story in the world.

What is this?

Soup is vegetables or pasta cooked in warm broth until the flavors share the water. The card shows golden soup with little round pieces floating like boats.

What does it mean?

Point to the soup is a search among bowls — and the floating pieces are the tell. Warm food also arrives with the room’s one safety ritual: the blow.

What does the child need to know?

Blowing is the rule and the skill: one gentle breath across the spoon, every time. The rule keeps little mouths safe and gives children something to enforce on everyone else.

Why this matters

Soup is the first course of sick days, winter nights and every grandma’s table — the fishing game turns the slowest meal into the busiest one.

What it teaches

Patience rituals, one-per-spoon fishing, and hot-food safety.

Words to learn

soupwarmblowspoonfloatbowl

Say this to your child

“Warm soup with little swimmers! First the rule: scoop... blow — whooo — gently! Now fish: one piece per spoon. What did you catch? A noodle boat! And another... fishing until the bowl is empty is the whole game.”

Step by step

  1. Show the card and count the floating pieces. Teach the blow: raise an imaginary spoon, blow one gentle breath — whooo — now it is ready. Fish for real: one piece per spoonful, named and counted as it lands. The fisher who empties the bowl piece by piece has practiced patience the entire meal.

Look closer at the picture

Watch the blow: a gust spills, a breath cools. The gentle breath is a real breath-control skill, and soup is its daily practice field.

Ask your child

What do we do before the first bite? What did your spoon catch? Is the soup warm or cold? How many did you fish?

What your child can say or do

Blow first! / I caught one. / Noodle boat. / All gone — I fished it.

Out in the real world

Soup waits at every winter table and every sick day — the blow rule rides along, enforced by the child on every grown-up in range.

Try it together

Spoon fishing derby: float three o-shaped cereal pieces in a dry bowl, fish one per scoop with a real spoon, and count the catch. The derby record gets retold all day.

Understanding check

Ask what we do before eating hot soup. Blow, cool it, one breath — any safety answer passes.

This lesson pairs with the Soup flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Cafeteria.
